title: Schedule useful work without breaking its contract
description: Switch scenarios to see how a workload deadline, approved locations, capacity, and grid forecast determine whether carbon-aware shifting is safe.

nodes.label: Workload request
nodes.detail: Declares resource demand, earliest start, completion deadline, approved data locations, retry safety, and the functional unit being measured.

nodes.label: Constraint-aware scheduler
nodes.detail: Rejects options that violate service, data, or capacity constraints before comparing expected emissions among feasible choices.

nodes.label: Grid forecast
nodes.detail: Provides time- and location-specific carbon-intensity estimates with an update time and forecast horizon. Realized intensity is recorded after execution.

nodes.label: Region A now
nodes.detail: Has approved data and capacity now, but the current grid intensity is higher than a later eligible window.

nodes.label: Region B later
nodes.detail: Offers a lower forecast intensity only if data residency, transfer cost, capacity, and completion deadline all permit the move.

nodes.label: Measured execution
nodes.detail: Records energy, realized grid intensity, allocated hardware impact, functional units, retries, completion time, and service quality.

nodes.label: Deadline fallback
nodes.detail: Runs in an approved location when waiting or moving would risk the product contract. Carbon awareness is bounded by this fallback.

scenarios.label: Flexible batch
scenarios.summary: A four-hour job may start within the next twelve hours in either approved region, and Region B has confirmed capacity before the deadline.
scenarios.result: Shift the job, then calculate the result from measured energy and realized grid intensity. Keep Region A as the deadline fallback if the forecast or capacity changes.

scenarios.label: Interactive request
scenarios.summary: A user-facing request has a 300 ms latency objective and no meaningful temporal flexibility.
scenarios.result: Serve the request now. Improve code, caching, and hardware efficiency instead of delaying user work for a cleaner forecast window.

scenarios.label: Residency constraint
scenarios.summary: Region B has lower forecast intensity, but the workload's regulated data is approved only for Region A.
scenarios.result: The lower-carbon location is infeasible. A scheduler must apply residency before optimization and record why the candidate was rejected.

scenarios.label: Forecast changes
scenarios.summary: The selected low-intensity window deteriorates and waiting longer would now threaten the completion deadline.
scenarios.result: Use the declared fallback and complete the useful work safely. Record forecast error and realized emissions so future scheduling policy can improve.
